blocks.explanation:
A secant term equals a linear term: a graphical-solution question, but the secant graph has asymptotes, so we must be careful.
We need every \(x\) in \([-\pi, \pi]\) where \(y = \sec(x + 3)\) meets \(y = -2x + \frac{1}{3}\).
Plan: find the asymptotes and branches, make a table, draw, read every crossing, refine and check.
steps:
Given: \(\sec(x + 3) = -2x + \frac{1}{3}\), \(x \in [-\pi, \pi]\).
To find: all \(x\) in the interval that satisfy it.
Method: Plot \(y = \sec(x + 3)\) and \(y = -2x + \frac{1}{3}\) on the same axes and read the intersections. Use \(d = \sec(x + 3) - (-2x + \frac{1}{3})\), but ignore sign changes that happen across an asymptote.

Asymptotes of \(y = \sec(x + 3)\)
\(\sec(x + 3) = \frac{1}{\cos(x + 3)}\) is undefined where \(\cos(x + 3) = 0\):
\[x + 3 = \tfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x \approx -1.43\]
\[x + 3 = \tfrac{3\pi}{2} \Rightarrow x \approx 1.71\]
Why: These are the only values of \(x + 3\) in \([3 - \pi, 3 + \pi]\) with cosine zero; there the graph shoots off to \(\pm\infty\).

The three branches
Left (\(-\pi \le x < -1.43\)): \(\cos(x + 3) > 0\), so \(\sec(x + 3) \ge 1\): a U shape rising to \(+\infty\).
Middle (\(-1.43 < x < 1.71\)): \(\cos(x + 3) < 0\), so \(\sec(x + 3) \le -1\): an upside-down U whose top is \((\pi - 3, -1) \approx (0.14, -1)\).
Right (\(1.71 < x \le \pi\)): again \(\sec(x + 3) \ge 1\).
The line \(y = -2x + \frac{1}{3}\) falls from \(6.62\) at \(x = -\pi\) to \(-5.95\) at \(x = \pi\).
Why: On the left branch the line (3.19 to 6.62) meets the rising U once. On the middle branch the line is below \(-1\) only when \(x > \frac{2}{3}\); there it dips just under the top of the upside-down U and cuts it twice. On the right branch \(y \ge 1\) but the line is below \(-3\): no meeting.

Draw both graphs and read the intersections
Draw the dashed asymptotes first, then the three branches and the line (see the figure). The graphs meet near
\[x \approx -1.70,\ 0.80,\ 1.22\]
Why: Three intersection points, so three roots. The two right-hand points are close together, so draw that part on a large scale.

answer_figure.alt: Graph of y = sec(x + 3) (blue) on minus pi to pi with dashed vertical asymptotes at x = pi/2 minus 3 (about minus 1.43) and x = 3pi/2 minus 3 (about 1.71): a U-shaped branch on the left rising to infinity, an upside-down U in the middle with top point (0.14, minus 1), and another U on the right. The falling line y = minus 2x + 1/3 (pink) cuts the left branch at x about minus 1.70 and the middle branch twice, at x about 0.80 and 1.22.
answer_figure.caption: Exercise 10.2 Q4: y = sec(x + 3) and y = −2x + 1/3 on [−π, π]; three intersections (original drawing)

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The answer key prints only \(x = -1.66\) radians. This is incomplete and inaccurate: at \(x = -1.66\), \(\sec(1.34) \approx 4.37\) but \(-2(-1.66) + \frac{1}{3} \approx 3.65\). The root on the left branch is \(x = -1.7003\ldots \approx -1.70\), and the line also cuts the middle branch twice, at \(x \approx 0.80\) and \(x \approx 1.22\). Correct answer: \(x \approx -1.70,\ 0.80,\ 1.22\) radians.
